Definition: from a derivative of G5324; (properly abstract) a (vain) show ("fantasy"):--pomp.
BiblicalUsage: Phantasia is a show, a pomp, a vain display, and it appears once, at Paul's hearing before Agrippa. The king and Bernice come with great pomp into the audience chamber, with the chief captains and principal men of the city, and Paul is brought forth in chains.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the pomp is the point: kings in their glory come to hear a prisoner, and the prisoner is the one with something to say.
RelatedEvents: Paul Before Felix, Festus, and Agrippa
